CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.retired_stage_to_canonical(old_stage text)
 RETURNS booking_stage
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
  select case old_stage
    when 'Quote'      then 'Quote'
    when 'Draft'      then 'Quote'
    when 'Confirmed'  then 'Booked'
    when 'Preparing'  then 'Booked'
    when 'Ready'      then 'Packed'
    when 'Dispatched' then 'Packed'
    when 'On Rent'    then 'On Rent'
    when 'Return Due' then 'On Rent'
    when 'Inspection' then 'Returned'
    when 'Cleaning'   then 'Returned'
    when 'Completed'  then 'Returned'
    when 'Closed'     then 'Closed'
    when 'Cancelled'  then 'Quote'
    else null
    -- NULL in, NULL out -- from_stage is legitimately null on a booking's
    -- first transition. Any other unmapped input is impossible today: every
    -- caller below passes a booking_stage-typed column cast to text, and
    -- that type had exactly these thirteen members, no others. A future
    -- caller feeding this function looser text (e.g. a go-live import) should
    -- reconsider this branch -- an unmapped non-null value here currently
    -- resolves to NULL rather than raising, which a NOT NULL column will
    -- catch loudly but a nullable one (from_stage) will not.
  end::booking_stage_v2;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.enforce_approver_is_actor()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth_user_id();
begin
  -- Only the moment of approval is governed.
  if new.approval_state = 'Approved'::damage_approval_state
     and old.approval_state is distinct from 'Approved'::damage_approval_state then

    if v_actor is null then
      raise exception
        'An approval must be attributable, and this session resolves to no user. Nothing was approved.'
        using errcode = 'check_violation';
    end if;

    if new.approved_by is distinct from v_actor then
      raise exception
        'approved_by must be the session performing the approval. Recording somebody else as the approver is not an approval, it is an assertion about them.'
        using errcode = 'check_violation';
    end if;
  end if;

  return new;
end $function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.set_staff_pin(p_pin text)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'extensions', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_user_id  uuid := auth_user_id();
  v_mobile   text;
  v_rotating boolean;
  v_pw_at    bigint;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    raise exception 'A PIN can only be set by a signed-in staff session.';
  end if;

  /*
   * ── the freshness gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   *
   * Minting a credential requires having proved identity RECENTLY, not merely
   * holding a session that proved it at some point.
   *
   * The attack this stops is mundane and is the likeliest one on this floor: an
   * unattended tablet with an hours-old session. Without this gate, anyone
   * walking past can silently add their OWN PIN to somebody else's account and
   * from then on re-open that session at will — a permanent credential minted
   * from a temporary opportunity, with the owner's name on every row it writes.
   *
   * ⚠ What this is NOT, and the spec for this feature got it wrong:
   *
   * The design asked that a PIN-unlocked session be forbidden from setting a
   * PIN. That is **not expressible here**, and the reason is structural: a PIN
   * unlock does not touch the JWT. `verify_staff_pin` returns a verdict, the
   * existing token is reused unchanged, and so a PIN-unlocked session presents
   * a token identical to the password sign-in that created it. The database
   * cannot tell them apart because there is nothing different to see.
   *
   * The freshness window is the honest approximation: it does not identify how
   * the curtain was opened, it bounds how long ago the password was typed. That
   * closes the unattended-tablet case, which is what the spec was reaching for.
   *
   * `amr` ("authentication methods references") is a GoTrue claim carrying one
   * entry per method used on this session with a unix timestamp — verified on
   * this project: {"aal":"aal1","amr":[{"method":"password","timestamp":...}]}.
   * Absent amr means this did not arrive as a GoTrue user request, so it is
   * refused rather than waved through: a service-role or psql caller is not a
   * staff member choosing their own PIN, and this function has no other purpose.
   */
  select max((entry ->> 'timestamp')::bigint)
    into v_pw_at
    from jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(auth.jwt() -> 'amr', '[]'::jsonb)) as entry
   where entry ->> 'method' = 'password';

  if v_pw_at is null or to_timestamp(v_pw_at) < now() - interval '15 minutes' then
    raise exception
      'For security, a PIN can only be set within 15 minutes of signing in with your password. Sign out and sign in again, then set the PIN.';
  end if;

  -- The staff row must exist and be active. An inactive identity does not get a
  -- fresh credential, and 0060's note is the reason this is checked here rather
  -- than assumed: an auth account can exist with no matching staff row at all.
  select mobile into v_mobile
    from users
   where id = v_user_id and is_active;

  if not found then
    raise exception 'No active staff row for this identity; a PIN cannot be set.';
  end if;

  -- Shape. Enforced here as well as in the UI because the RPC is reachable
  -- without the numpad.
  if p_pin is null or p_pin !~ '^[0-9]{6}$' then
    raise exception 'A PIN must be exactly 6 digits.';
  end if;

  -- Weak-PIN rejection. Six identical digits, six sequential in either
  -- direction, and the last four of the mobile on the staff row — the three
  -- guesses someone standing at a shared tablet actually makes.
  if p_pin ~ '^(.)\1{5}$' then
    raise exception 'That PIN is six identical digits. Choose another.';
  end if;

  if strpos('01234567890', p_pin) > 0 or strpos('09876543210', p_pin) > 0 then
    raise exception 'That PIN is six sequential digits. Choose another.';
  end if;

  if v_mobile is not null
     and length(regexp_replace(v_mobile, '\D', '', 'g')) >= 4
     and right(regexp_replace(v_mobile, '\D', '', 'g'), 4) = right(p_pin, 4) then
    raise exception 'That PIN ends with the last four digits of your mobile number. Choose another.';
  end if;

  -- Rotation is a revoke plus an insert, never an UPDATE of pin_hash. Law 3:
  -- the fact that a different PIN was in force until now survives.
  update staff_auth_pins
     set revoked_at = now(),
         revoked_by = v_user_id
   where user_id = v_user_id
     and revoked_at is null;

  -- Captured explicitly rather than reading FOUND at the insert. FOUND would
  -- still be the UPDATE's result there and would work, but it is one statement
  -- away from silently meaning something else.
  v_rotating := found;

  insert into staff_auth_pins (user_id, pin_hash, rotated_at)
  values (
    v_user_id,
    extensions.crypt(p_pin, extensions.gen_salt('bf', 10)),
    case when v_rotating then now() else null end
  );
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.recalculate_invoice_totals()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_subtotal numeric(14,2);
  v_discount_pct numeric(5,2);
  v_vat_rate numeric(5,4);
  v_discount numeric(14,2);
  v_taxable numeric(14,2);
  v_vat numeric(14,2);
  v_total numeric(14,2);
  v_paid numeric(14,2);
  v_target_invoice_id uuid;
begin
  if (TG_OP = 'DELETE') then
    v_target_invoice_id := OLD.invoice_id;
  else
    v_target_invoice_id := NEW.invoice_id;
  end if;

  -- 1. The subtotal is the sum of the lines. Not rounded — money.ts does not
  --    round it either, and rounding it here would silently move money that no
  --    line accounts for.
  select coalesce(sum(line_total), 0)
    into v_subtotal
    from invoice_lines
   where invoice_id = v_target_invoice_id;

  -- 2. The header inputs. STRICT: a missing invoice raises rather than pricing
  --    at zero VAT (0079's reasoning, kept). vat_rate is NOT NULL, so it needs
  --    no fallback — see §2 of the header.
  --
  --    `paid_amount` is READ here, not re-derived from `payments`. That is
  --    deliberate and it matters: this function is invoker-rights and runs as
  --    whoever wrote the line. Under Law 6 the floor roles are held off the
  --    money tables, so calling invoice_paid_net() here would make appending a
  --    damage line at return (R-03) fail with `permission denied for table
  --    payments` for exactly the staff who append it. The stored column is
  --    authoritative because 0087 rewrites it on every payment and every
  --    reversal; this path consumes it rather than competing with it.
  select discount_percent, vat_rate, coalesce(paid_amount, 0)
    into strict v_discount_pct, v_vat_rate, v_paid
    from invoices
   where id = v_target_invoice_id;

  -- 3. money.ts `price()`, step for step. Two rounds, not four: `taxable` and
  --    `total` are exact sums of already-rounded terms in the engine and are
  --    exact sums here. See the header for why this departs from §2.2's sketch.
  v_discount := invoice_discount_amount(v_subtotal, v_discount_pct);
  v_taxable  := v_subtotal - v_discount;
  v_vat      := invoice_vat_amount(v_taxable, v_vat_rate);
  v_total    := v_taxable + v_vat;

  -- 4. MONEY-04. Split the subtraction into its two floored halves, through the
  --    same two functions the payment path uses, so an overpayment neither
  --    vanishes nor trips invoices_amounts_non_negative. Before this, live ran
  --    `v_outstanding := v_total - v_paid` unfloored and an overpaid invoice
  --    raised 23514 HERE, refusing the line — including the damage line at
  --    return, which is the charge R-03 exists to add.
  --
  -- 5. One UPDATE, so the row is never briefly inconsistent and the audit trail
  --    carries one event per line change rather than two.
  --    `paid_amount` is not written: it is the payment path's column (0087).
  --    `status` is not written either — R-14 (a Draft is sticky) and R-04 (an
  --    issued invoice's figures are immutable) both live elsewhere, and a line
  --    edit is not an issue action.
  update invoices
     set subtotal           = v_subtotal,
         discount_amount    = v_discount,
         taxable_amount     = v_taxable,
         vat_amount         = v_vat,
         total_amount       = v_total,
         outstanding_amount = invoice_outstanding(v_total, v_paid),
         credit_amount      = invoice_credit(v_total, v_paid),
         updated_at         = now()
   where id = v_target_invoice_id;

  return null;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.log_audit_event()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_actor_id uuid;
  v_client_uuid uuid := gen_random_uuid();
  v_action audit_action;
  v_event_class audit_event_class := 'status change';
  v_category audit_category := 'Rentals';
  v_module audit_module := 'Rentals';
  -- Column-safe reads: NULL when the table does not define the column, instead
  -- of a 42703 that aborts the caller's statement.
  v_row_created_by uuid := nullif(to_jsonb(NEW) ->> 'created_by', '')::uuid;
  v_row_updated_by uuid := nullif(to_jsonb(NEW) ->> 'updated_by', '')::uuid;
begin
  -- Resolve actor from session setting or default to system
  begin
    v_actor_id := nullif(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '')::uuid;
  exception when others then
    v_actor_id := null;
  end;

  if (TG_OP = 'INSERT') then
    v_action := 'Create';
    insert into audit_events (
      client_uuid,
      event_class,
      category,
      module,
      action,
      severity,
      status,
      table_name,
      record_id,
      actor_id,
      new_values
    ) values (
      v_client_uuid,
      v_event_class,
      v_category,
      v_module,
      v_action,
      'Informational',
      'Success',
      TG_TABLE_NAME,
      NEW.id,
      coalesce(v_row_created_by, v_actor_id),
      to_jsonb(NEW)
    );
    return NEW;
  elsif (TG_OP = 'UPDATE') then
    v_action := 'Update';
    insert into audit_events (
      client_uuid,
      event_class,
      category,
      module,
      action,
      severity,
      status,
      table_name,
      record_id,
      actor_id,
      old_values,
      new_values
    ) values (
      v_client_uuid,
      v_event_class,
      v_category,
      v_module,
      v_action,
      'Informational',
      'Success',
      TG_TABLE_NAME,
      NEW.id,
      coalesce(v_row_updated_by, v_actor_id),
      to_jsonb(OLD),
      to_jsonb(NEW)
    );
    return NEW;
  end if;

  return null;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.record_password_reset_request(p_user_id uuid)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth_user_id();
  v_email text;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'Recording a reset request requires a signed-in session.';
  end if;

  if auth_user_role() <> 'Owner' then
    raise exception 'Only the Owner may request a password reset for another staff member (rbac.canManageSettings).';
  end if;

  select email into v_email from users where id = p_user_id;

  if not found then
    raise exception 'No staff row for that identity; nothing to record.';
  end if;

  insert into audit_events (
    client_uuid,
    event_class,
    category,
    module,
    action,
    severity,
    status,
    table_name,
    record_id,
    actor_id,
    actor_role,
    new_values,
    reason
  )
  values (
    gen_random_uuid(),
    'session',
    'Authentication',
    'Authentication',
    -- NOT 'Password Changed'. No password changed; a link was requested. The
    -- enum has the stronger label and using it would be the easy lie.
    'Update',
    -- A credential recovery path is not routine traffic. It is the action an
    -- attacker with an Owner session would reach for first.
    'High',
    'Success',
    'users',
    p_user_id,
    v_actor,
    auth_user_role()::system_role,
    jsonb_build_object('reset_link_requested_for', v_email),
    format('Password reset link requested for %s. Requested, not confirmed delivered — GoTrue cannot report delivery.', v_email)
  );
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.invoice_outstanding(p_total numeric, p_paid numeric)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
  /* MONEY-04. THE outstanding rule. Floored, because
     invoices_amounts_non_negative CHECKs outstanding_amount >= 0 and because a
     negative receivable is a credit, which has its own column. */
  select greatest(coalesce(p_total, 0) - coalesce(p_paid, 0), 0);
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.invoice_credit(p_total numeric, p_paid numeric)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
  /* MONEY-04. The other side of the same subtraction, so the money the floor
     above removes is not lost. */
  select greatest(coalesce(p_paid, 0) - coalesce(p_total, 0), 0);
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.set_updated_at()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
begin
  -- Unconditional, and deliberately so. The device supplying a value is the
  -- defect (§4.43(d).1), so a supplied value carries no authority here.
  new.updated_at := now();
  return new;
end;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.bump_row_version()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
begin
  -- old.version is never null: the column is `not null default 1` with
  -- `check (version >= 1)`, so this cannot produce a null and cannot go below 1.
  new.version := old.version + 1;
  return new;
end;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.invoice_discount_amount(p_subtotal numeric, p_discount_percent numeric)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
  /* money.ts:135 — toWholeRupee(subtotal * (discountPercent / 100)).
     discount_percent is a PERCENT, so it divides by 100. */
  select round(coalesce(p_subtotal, 0) * (coalesce(p_discount_percent, 0) / 100.0), 0);
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.invoice_vat_amount(p_taxable numeric, p_vat_rate numeric)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
  /* money.ts:137 — toWholeRupee(taxable * (vatPercent / 100)).
     invoices.vat_rate is a FRACTION — numeric(5,4), thirteen percent stored as
     four decimal places — NOT a percent, so there is no division here.
     The hardcoded rate this replaces is deliberately not written anywhere in
     this function, not even in a comment: post-condition (5) greps prosrc for
     it, and a comment mentioning it fails this migration. */
  select round(coalesce(p_taxable, 0) * coalesce(p_vat_rate, 0), 0);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.create_invoice(p_payload jsonb)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_client_uuid  uuid    := (p_payload ->> 'client_uuid')::uuid;
  v_actor        uuid    := (p_payload ->> 'created_by')::uuid;
  v_booking_no   text    := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_payload ->> 'booking_no', '')), '');
  v_booking_key  uuid    := (p_payload ->> 'booking_id')::uuid;
  v_vat_rate     numeric := (p_payload ->> 'vat_rate')::numeric;
  v_notes        text    := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_payload ->> 'notes', '')), '');
  v_role         system_role;
  v_existing     invoices%rowtype;
  v_booking_id   uuid;
  v_resolved_no  text;
  v_client_id    uuid;
  v_branch_id    uuid;
  v_cancelled    timestamptz;
  v_terms        text;
  v_term_days    integer;
  v_due_date     date;
  v_discounts    integer;
  v_booking_vat_rate numeric(5,4);
  v_percent      numeric := 0;
  v_prior        record;
  v_invoice_id   uuid;
  v_line_count   integer := 0;
  v_written      integer;
  v_totals       invoices%rowtype;
begin
  -- ── Rights, first, before anything is read ────────────────────────────────
  -- R-05: Owner · Admin · Manager · Accounts may raise an invoice. This is the
  -- gate, because definer rights mean RLS will not be. It repeats 0086's four
  -- policies on purpose; the post-conditions below prove the two agree by
  -- calling this function as a Coordinator and as Warehouse.
  v_role := auth_user_role();
  if v_role is null or v_role not in ('Owner', 'Admin', 'Manager', 'Accounts') then
    raise exception
      'create_invoice: this session (%) may not raise an invoice. R-05 gives that to Owner, Admin, Manager and Accounts. Nothing was created.',
      coalesce(v_role::text, 'unidentified')
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  -- Law 6. Redundant while auth_can_view_money() excludes exactly the roles
  -- R-05 omits, and kept so that it stays true if either definition moves. A
  -- money-blind caller is refused by name rather than billing zero.
  if not auth_can_view_money() then
    raise exception
      'create_invoice: this session cannot read money (Law 6), so the invoice it raised would bill nothing. Nothing was created.'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if v_client_uuid is null then
    raise exception 'create_invoice: client_uuid is required (Law 8 — every write carries one)';
  end if;
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'create_invoice: created_by is required; there is no system actor';
  end if;

  -- ── Law 8 replay check, BEFORE anything is written ────────────────────────
  select * into v_existing from invoices where client_uuid = v_client_uuid;
  if found then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'invoice_id',      v_existing.id,
      'invoice_no',      v_existing.invoice_no,
      'status',          v_existing.status,
      'booking_id',      v_existing.booking_id,
      'booking_no',      (select booking_no from bookings where id = v_existing.booking_id),
      'client_id',       v_existing.client_id,
      'due_date',        v_existing.due_date,
      'line_count',      (select count(*) from invoice_lines where invoice_id = v_existing.id),
      'subtotal',        v_existing.subtotal,
      'discount_amount', v_existing.discount_amount,
      'taxable_amount',  v_existing.taxable_amount,
      'vat_amount',      v_existing.vat_amount,
      'total',           v_existing.total_amount,
      'replayed',        true
    );
  end if;

  -- ── The booking this bills ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Either key is accepted; `booking_no` is what the operator saw on screen and
  -- what the action holds, `booking_id` is what a server-side caller holds.
  if v_booking_key is null and v_booking_no is null then
    raise exception 'create_invoice: an invoice must name the booking it bills (booking_id or booking_no).';
  end if;

  select b.id, b.booking_no, b.client_id, b.branch_id, b.cancelled_at
    into v_booking_id, v_resolved_no, v_client_id, v_branch_id, v_cancelled
    from bookings b
   where (v_booking_key is not null and b.id = v_booking_key)
      or (v_booking_key is null and b.booking_no = v_booking_no);

  if not found then
    raise exception
      'create_invoice: no booking % exists, so there is nothing to invoice and nothing was created.',
      coalesce(v_booking_key::text, v_booking_no);
  end if;

  -- A cancelled booking is not invoiced from here. Whether a cancellation
  -- carries a fee is explicitly unruled (PLAN.md §4.16), so this refuses rather
  -- than deciding it — the same position `createInvoice.ts` took.
  if v_cancelled is not null then
    raise exception
      'create_invoice: booking % was cancelled on %. Whether a cancellation carries a fee is an open ruling (PLAN.md §4.16), so nothing was created.',
      v_resolved_no, v_cancelled::date;
  end if;

  -- ── R-03 · one invoice per rental ─────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Checked after the replay check, so a genuine retry of the same press is a
  -- replay and only a SECOND intent is refused. Refuses on ANY existing
  -- invoice including a voided one, which is stricter than SPEC-P0-1 §3.1's
  -- "no non-Void invoice": the line keys are the booking rows' own client_uuids
  -- (see the header), so a second invoice over the same booking would collide
  -- on invoice_lines_client_uuid_key partway through. Re-invoicing after a void
  -- needs its own key strategy and its own ruling; refusing is the honest
  -- interim. TODO(decision) — re-invoicing a booking whose only invoice was
  -- voided (MONEY-07).
  -- Aliased so the record's field names are unmistakable; an unaliased
  -- `status::text` is still called `status`, which reads like the column and is
  -- not one.
  select invoice_no as prior_no, status::text as prior_status into v_prior
    from invoices where booking_id = v_booking_id limit 1;
  if found then
    raise exception
      'create_invoice: booking % already has an invoice (%, %). One invoice per rental — damage and late fees append as lines to the existing Draft, and corrections after issue are Void + Credit Note. Nothing was created.',
      v_resolved_no, coalesce(v_prior.prior_no, 'a Draft'), v_prior.prior_status;
  end if;

  -- ── The due date, from the client's payment terms ─────────────────────────
  -- `clients.payment_terms` is an enum whose labels ARE the rule; this is not a
  -- policy decision restated in SQL. NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Immediate', so the
  -- coalesce is a belt, and Immediate (due today) is the safe direction: it is
  -- visible and correctable, where a wrong 30 grants credit nobody agreed to.
  select payment_terms::text into v_terms from clients where id = v_client_id;
  v_term_days := case coalesce(v_terms, 'Immediate')
                   when '7 days'  then 7
                   when '15 days' then 15
                   when '30 days' then 30
                   else 0
                 end;
  v_due_date := current_date + v_term_days;

  -- Several audited discount rows add into one invoice discount percentage.
  select count(*), coalesce(sum(percent),0)
    into v_discounts, v_percent
    from public.booking_discounts where booking_id=v_booking_id;
  if v_percent < 0 or v_percent > 100 then
    raise exception 'Invalid booking discount %', v_percent using errcode='23514';
  end if;
  -- New bookings pin a VAT fraction; legacy bookings retain supplied invoice VAT.
  select b.vat_rate into v_booking_vat_rate from public.bookings b where b.id=v_booking_id;
  -- The booking's pinned tax mode is authoritative, including zero VAT.
  -- The caller's current Settings value might have changed since the Quote;
  -- do not let the later device setting reprice the client's agreed booking.
  if v_booking_vat_rate is not null then
    v_vat_rate:=v_booking_vat_rate;
  end if;
  -- ── The header ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- `invoice_no` and `issue_date` are OMITTED, not set to null: the column list
  -- is what documents the intent (R-15). 0086 makes both nullable and adds
  -- `invoices_issued_together` so a half-issued row cannot exist.
  -- The money columns keep their zero defaults; the trigger owns them.
  insert into invoices (
    client_uuid, booking_id, client_id, branch_id, status,
    due_date, currency, discount_percent, vat_rate, notes,
    created_by, updated_by
  )
  values (
    v_client_uuid,
    v_booking_id,
    v_client_id,
    v_branch_id,
    'Draft',
    v_due_date,
    'NPR',
    coalesce(v_percent, 0),
    -- numeric(5,4) — a FRACTION, not a percentage. 13% arrives as 0.1300.
    coalesce(v_vat_rate, 0.1300),
    v_notes,
    v_actor,
    v_actor
  )
  returning id into v_invoice_id;

  -- ── The lines: a snapshot, not a join ─────────────────────────────────────
  -- SPEC-P0-1 §3.1: the rate card is pinned per booking, so the figures are
  -- COPIED here and never re-derived from `products` afterwards.
  --
  -- `line_total` carries each line's NET figure, because
  -- `recalculate_invoice_totals` derives the subtotal as `sum(line_total)`. The
  -- booking-level percentage is applied on top by the trigger from the header's
  -- `discount_percent`; `invoice_lines.discount_percent` stays 0, because the
  -- line's own discount is already inside its total and counting it twice would
  -- discount twice.

  -- (1) Equipment and bundles, from `booking_lines`.
  -- The mapping is `LINE_KIND_BY_TYPE` from createInvoice.ts, moved next to the
  -- enums it maps. Every member of `booking_line_type` is named and the CASE
  -- has **no ELSE on purpose**: if `booking_line_type` ever grows a member,
  -- this yields NULL, `invoice_lines.line_kind` is NOT NULL, and the whole
  -- transaction aborts with nothing written. That is the safe direction. The
  -- TypeScript it replaces fell through a `?? 'Equipment Rental'`, so an
  -- accessory or an ad-hoc line was billed as equipment rental with nothing
  -- said about it.
  -- ⚠ `line_kind` has no `Damage` and no `Missing` member, so a damage charge
  -- cannot become an invoice line at all. That is MONEY-08; widening the enum
  -- is a ruling (it decides deposit-versus-invoice precedence too) and is NOT
  -- done here.
  -- Law 3 keeps a voided booking line in its table; a voided line is not
  -- billable, so it is kept off the bill.
  insert into invoice_lines (
    client_uuid, invoice_id, line_kind, description,
    quantity, days, unit_rate, line_total, discount_percent, sort_order,
    price_breakdown
  )
  select
    bl.client_uuid,
    v_invoice_id,
    (case bl.line_type
       when 'Equipment'   then 'Equipment Rental'
       when 'Bundle'      then 'Equipment Rental'
       when 'Accessory'   then 'Equipment Rental'
       when 'Manual item' then 'Equipment Rental'
       when 'Service'     then 'Services'
       when 'Sub-rental'  then 'Sub-Rental'
     end)::line_kind,
    -- `booking_lines.description` is nullable and `invoice_lines.description`
    -- is NOT NULL. The line type is the honest fallback: it says what the
    -- charge is for without inventing a product name nobody typed.
    coalesce(nullif(btrim(bl.description), ''), bl.line_type::text),
    greatest(1, bl.qty),
    greatest(1, bl.days),
    bl.rate,
    coalesce(bl.line_total, greatest(0, greatest(1, bl.qty) * greatest(1, bl.days) * bl.rate - coalesce(bl.discount_amount, 0))),
    0,
    coalesce(bl.sort_order, 0),
    bl.price_breakdown
  from booking_lines bl
  where bl.booking_id = v_booking_id
    and bl.voided_at is null;
  get diagnostics v_written = row_count;
  v_line_count := v_line_count + v_written;

  -- (2) Crew, from `booking_crew_lines` — a different table, which is why it
  -- was billed to nobody until 4 Sep. Overtime, accommodation and meals are
  -- per-engagement totals, not per day; folding them into the unit rate keeps
  -- quantity × days × rate equal to the crew member's true cost, which is the
  -- arithmetic the recalc trigger applies to every line without exception.
  --
  -- `line_total` is computed EXACTLY (day_rate × days + extras) rather than
  -- from the divided unit rate, and that distinction earns its keep:
  -- `unit_rate` is `numeric(14,2)`, so a gaffer at 8000 × 3 days plus 4000 of
  -- extras stores a unit rate of 9333.33 whose product with days is 27,999.99
  -- — a rupee short of the 28,000 owed. `line_total` is what
  -- `recalculate_invoice_totals` sums, so the bill is exact and only the
  -- displayed per-day rate carries the rounding. Verified against the same
  -- reference figures the TypeScript suite used to pin (28,000 / 18,000 /
  -- 4,200), so this snapshot bills what its predecessor billed.
  insert into invoice_lines (
    client_uuid, invoice_id, line_kind, description,
    quantity, days, unit_rate, line_total, discount_percent, sort_order
  )
  select
    cl.client_uuid,
    v_invoice_id,
    'Crew Charges'::line_kind,
    coalesce(
      nullif(btrim(concat_ws(' - ', nullif(btrim(cl.name), ''), cl.crew_role::text)), ''),
      'Crew'
    ),
    1,
    greatest(1, cl.days),
    cl.day_rate
      + (coalesce(cl.overtime, 0) + coalesce(cl.accommodation, 0) + coalesce(cl.meals, 0))
        / greatest(1, cl.days),
    cl.day_rate * greatest(1, cl.days)
      + coalesce(cl.overtime, 0) + coalesce(cl.accommodation, 0) + coalesce(cl.meals, 0),
    0,
    1000 + (row_number() over (order by cl.created_at, cl.id))::integer - 1
  from booking_crew_lines cl
  where cl.booking_id = v_booking_id
    and cl.voided_at is null;
  get diagnostics v_written = row_count;
  v_line_count := v_line_count + v_written;

  -- (3) Transport, from `booking_transport`. A row carrying no charge is a
  -- logistics record, not a bill line, so it is skipped rather than billed at
  -- zero. `booking_transport` has no `voided_at` column — there is nothing to
  -- exclude on.
  insert into invoice_lines (
    client_uuid, invoice_id, line_kind, description,
    quantity, days, unit_rate, line_total, discount_percent, sort_order
  )
  select
    bt.client_uuid,
    v_invoice_id,
    'Transport'::line_kind,
    case
      when nullif(btrim(coalesce(bt.vehicle, '')), '') is not null
        then 'Transport - ' || btrim(bt.vehicle)
      else 'Transport'
    end,
    1,
    1,
    coalesce(bt.delivery_charge, 0) + coalesce(bt.fuel_charge, 0),
    coalesce(bt.delivery_charge, 0) + coalesce(bt.fuel_charge, 0),
    0,
    2000 + (row_number() over (order by bt.created_at, bt.id))::integer - 1
  from booking_transport bt
  where bt.booking_id = v_booking_id
    and coalesce(bt.delivery_charge, 0) + coalesce(bt.fuel_charge, 0) > 0;
  get diagnostics v_written = row_count;
  v_line_count := v_line_count + v_written;

  -- ── The totals, as POSTGRES computed them ─────────────────────────────────
  -- Re-read, never derived here. A caller rendering its own figure is showing
  -- an estimate; this is the row.
  select * into v_totals from invoices where id = v_invoice_id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'invoice_id',      v_totals.id,
    -- R-15 — stated rather than omitted, so a caller cannot mistake a missing
    -- field for a number it failed to read.
    'invoice_no',      v_totals.invoice_no,
    'status',          v_totals.status,
    'booking_id',      v_booking_id,
    'booking_no',      v_resolved_no,
    'client_id',       v_client_id,
    'due_date',        v_totals.due_date,
    'line_count',      v_line_count,
    'subtotal',        v_totals.subtotal,
    'discount_amount', v_totals.discount_amount,
    'taxable_amount',  v_totals.taxable_amount,
    'vat_amount',      v_totals.vat_amount,
    'total',           v_totals.total_amount,
    'replayed',        false
  );
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.reservations_follow_stage_transition()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_pickup    timestamptz;
  v_return    timestamptz;
  v_period    tstzrange;
  v_booking_no text;
  v_uncovered text;
begin
  -- ── Release paths ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Returned and Closed end the commitment; Quote un-makes it (see the header).
  -- Filtered on `released_at is null` so Returned -> Closed is a no-op rather
  -- than a second release that would overwrite the first reason.
  if NEW.to_stage in ('Returned', 'Closed', 'Quote') then
    update inventory_reservations
       set released_at     = NEW.occurred_at,
           released_reason = case NEW.to_stage
             when 'Returned' then 'Released on Return: the booking reached Returned.'
             when 'Closed'   then 'Released on Close: the booking reached Closed.'
             else 'Released by a reversal back to Quote: a Quote holds nothing.'
           end
     where booking_id = NEW.booking_id
       and released_at is null;
    return NEW;
  end if;

  if NEW.to_stage <> 'Booked' then
    return NEW;
  end if;

  -- ── Booked: place the holds ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  select pickup_at, return_at, booking_no
    into v_pickup, v_return, v_booking_no
    from bookings
   where id = NEW.booking_id;

  if v_pickup is null then
    -- Unreachable through `apply_booking_stage_transition`, which raises on a
    -- missing booking before this trigger runs. Stated rather than assumed: if
    -- RLS ever hides the row from the caller, this must refuse, not reserve a
    -- null window.
    raise exception
      'Reservation rejected: booking % could not be read, so its rental window is unknown.',
      NEW.booking_id;
  end if;

  -- Half-open, matching `RENTAL_WINDOW_BOUNDS = 'half-open'` in
  -- `src/lib/availability.ts` (ruled PLAN.md §4.30(b)). A 12 Sep return and a
  -- 12 Sep pickup on the same unit do not collide. **Never change one of these
  -- two without the other** — the app would then check a different question
  -- from the one the constraint answers.
  v_period := tstzrange(v_pickup, v_return, '[)');

  -- Serialised: one row per live assigned unit.
  insert into inventory_reservations
    (client_uuid, booking_id, booking_line_id, asset_id, qty, period, created_by)
  select gen_random_uuid(), NEW.booking_id, bl.id, blu.asset_id, 1, v_period, NEW.actor_id
    from booking_lines bl
    join booking_line_units blu on blu.booking_line_id = bl.id
   where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
     and bl.voided_at is null
     and blu.released_at is null;

  -- Quantity: the remainder of each line that its units do not cover.
  -- `client_uuid` is minted PER ROW — it is UNIQUE on this table, so one key
  -- across several rows collides on the second.
  insert into inventory_reservations
    (client_uuid, booking_id, booking_line_id, product_id, qty, period, created_by)
  select gen_random_uuid(), NEW.booking_id, bl.id, bl.product_id, bl.qty - coalesce(u.n, 0),
         v_period, NEW.actor_id
    from booking_lines bl
    left join lateral (
      select count(*) as n
        from booking_line_units blu
       where blu.booking_line_id = bl.id
         and blu.released_at is null
    ) u on true
   where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
     and bl.voided_at is null
     and bl.product_id is not null
     and bl.qty - coalesce(u.n, 0) > 0;

  -- ── Coverage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Every live line that names stock now holds something. This is the check
  -- that turns a SECURITY INVOKER read the caller could not fully see into a
  -- refusal instead of a booking that commits gear it never reserved.
  select string_agg(bl.description, ', ')
    into v_uncovered
    from booking_lines bl
   where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
     and bl.voided_at is null
     and bl.product_id is not null
     and not exists (
       select 1 from inventory_reservations r
        where r.booking_line_id = bl.id
          and r.released_at is null
     );

  if v_uncovered is not null then
    raise exception
      'Reservation rejected: booking % reached Booked with no hold behind %. Nothing was booked.',
      coalesce(v_booking_no, NEW.booking_id::text), v_uncovered;
  end if;

  return NEW;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.release_reservations_on_cancellation()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
begin
  update inventory_reservations
     set released_at     = NEW.cancelled_at,
         released_reason = 'Released on cancellation of booking ' || NEW.booking_no || ': '
                           || coalesce(nullif(btrim(NEW.cancellation_reason), ''), 'no reason recorded')
   where booking_id = NEW.id
     and released_at is null;
  return NEW;
end;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.preventive_service_resets_the_meter()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
begin
  -- SECURITY DEFINER, for the same reason 0045's ceiling is: a Technician
  -- completing a job must be able to move the baseline on the unit even where
  -- `product_units_update` does not admit them, and the value written is read
  -- from the unit itself rather than supplied by the caller — so definer rights
  -- grant no ability to state a number.
  update product_units pu
     set service_meter_baseline = pu.running_hours
   where pu.id = NEW.product_unit_id;
  return NEW;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.open_missing_case_on_return()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_missing_count integer;
  v_client_id     uuid;
  v_client_name   text;
  v_booking_no    text;
  v_case_no       text;
  v_year          integer := extract(year from current_date);
  v_next_val      bigint;
begin
  -- Only trigger on transition to 'Returned'
  if NEW.to_stage <> 'Returned' then
    return NEW;
  end if;

  -- Count unreturned units for this booking
  select count(*) into v_missing_count
    from booking_lines bl
    join booking_line_units blu on blu.booking_line_id = bl.id
   where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
     and bl.voided_at is null
     and blu.returned_at is null;

  if v_missing_count > 0 then
    -- Do not open duplicate Missing cases for the same booking
    if not exists (
      select 1 from cases
       where linked_booking_id = NEW.booking_id
         and type = 'Missing'
    ) then
      select b.client_id, coalesce(c.name, 'Client'), b.booking_no
        into v_client_id, v_client_name, v_booking_no
        from bookings b
        left join clients c on c.id = b.client_id
       where b.id = NEW.booking_id;

      -- Generate next sequential CASE-YYYY-NNNN number
      select coalesce(max(substring(case_no from 11)::bigint), 0) + 1
        into v_next_val
        from cases
       where case_no ~ ('^CASE-' || v_year::text || '-[0-9]+$');

      v_case_no := 'CASE-' || v_year::text || '-' || lpad(v_next_val::text, 4, '0');

      insert into cases (
        client_uuid,
        case_no,
        type,
        title,
        counterparty_kind,
        counterparty_name,
        priority,
        status,
        linked_booking_id,
        owner_id,
        created_by
      ) values (
        gen_random_uuid(),
        v_case_no,
        'Missing',
        'Missing gear from booking ' || coalesce(v_booking_no, NEW.booking_id::text) || ' (' || v_missing_count::text || ' unreturned item' || case when v_missing_count = 1 then '' else 's' end || ')',
        'Client',
        v_client_name,
        'High',
        'Open',
        NEW.booking_id,
        NEW.actor_id,
        NEW.actor_id
      );
    end if;
  end if;

  return NEW;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.write_reservations_on_stage_transition()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_pickup     timestamptz;
  v_return     timestamptz;
  v_period     tstzrange;
  v_booking_no text;
begin
  -- ── Release paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if NEW.to_stage in ('Returned', 'Closed', 'Quote') then
    update inventory_reservations r
       set released_at     = NEW.occurred_at,
           released_reason = case NEW.to_stage
             when 'Returned' then 'Released on Return: the booking reached Returned.'
             when 'Closed'   then 'Released on Close: the booking reached Closed.'
             else 'Released by a reversal back to Quote: a Quote holds nothing.'
           end
     where booking_id = NEW.booking_id
       and released_at is null
       and (
         NEW.to_stage <> 'Returned'
         or r.asset_id is null
         or not exists (
           select 1 from booking_line_units blu
           join booking_lines bl on bl.id = blu.booking_line_id
           where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
             and blu.asset_id = r.asset_id
             and (blu.unit_state = 'Missing' or blu.returned_at is null)
         )
       );
    return NEW;
  end if;

  if NEW.to_stage <> 'Booked' then
    return NEW;
  end if;

  -- ── Booked: place the holds ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  select pickup_at, return_at, booking_no
    into v_pickup, v_return, v_booking_no
    from bookings
   where id = NEW.booking_id;

  if v_pickup is null then
    raise exception 'Reservation rejected: booking % has no pickup_at / return_at window.', NEW.booking_id;
  end if;

  v_period := tstzrange(v_pickup, v_return, '[)');

  -- Holds for serialised units
  insert into inventory_reservations
    (client_uuid, booking_id, booking_line_id, asset_id, period, created_by)
  select
    gen_random_uuid(),
    NEW.booking_id,
    blu.booking_line_id,
    blu.asset_id,
    v_period,
    NEW.actor_id
  from booking_line_units blu
  join booking_lines bl on bl.id = blu.booking_line_id
  join products p on p.id = bl.product_id
  where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
    and bl.voided_at is null
    and blu.asset_id is not null
    and p.tracking_mode = 'Serialised';

  -- Holds for non-serialised quantity lines
  insert into inventory_reservations
    (client_uuid, booking_id, booking_line_id, product_id, qty, period, created_by)
  select
    gen_random_uuid(),
    NEW.booking_id,
    bl.id,
    bl.product_id,
    bl.qty,
    v_period,
    NEW.actor_id
  from booking_lines bl
  join products p on p.id = bl.product_id
  where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
    and bl.voided_at is null
    and p.tracking_mode <> 'Serialised';

  return NEW;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.reservations_follow_booking_dates()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_new_period tstzrange;
begin
  -- Only act when rental boundaries actually change
  if (OLD.pickup_at is distinct from NEW.pickup_at) or (OLD.return_at is distinct from NEW.return_at) then
    if NEW.pickup_at is null or NEW.return_at is null then
      raise exception
        'Booking %: pickup_at and return_at cannot be null for an active rental.',
        NEW.booking_no;
    end if;

    if NEW.pickup_at >= NEW.return_at then
      raise exception
        'Booking %: pickup_at (%) must be strictly before return_at (%).',
        NEW.booking_no, NEW.pickup_at, NEW.return_at;
    end if;

    -- Half-open bounds '[)', strictly matching RENTAL_WINDOW_BOUNDS in src/lib/availability.ts
    v_new_period := tstzrange(NEW.pickup_at, NEW.return_at, '[)');

    -- Atomically update all unreleased holds for this booking.
    -- If the new period conflicts, GiST exclusion (0003) or capacity ceiling (0045)
    -- will raise an exception and roll back this entire UPDATE transaction.
    update public.inventory_reservations
       set period = v_new_period
     where booking_id = NEW.id
       and released_at is null
       and period is distinct from v_new_period;
  end if;

  return NEW;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.deduct_consumable_stock_on_handover()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_line       record;
  v_before     integer;
  v_after      integer;
begin
  -- Only trigger on transition to 'On Rent' (Handover complete)
  if NEW.to_stage <> 'On Rent' then
    return NEW;
  end if;

  -- Every Consumable-tracked line on this booking that hasn't already been
  -- deducted (the unique constraint on booking_line_id is the real guard;
  -- this check just avoids a wasted attempt on a re-run).
  for v_line in
    select bl.id as booking_line_id, bl.product_id, bl.qty
    from booking_lines bl
    join products p on p.id = bl.product_id
    where bl.booking_id = NEW.booking_id
      and bl.voided_at is null
      and p.tracking_mode = 'Consumable'
      and not exists (
        select 1 from consumable_stock_movements csm
        where csm.booking_line_id = bl.id
      )
  loop
    select total_quantity into v_before
      from products
     where id = v_line.product_id
       for update;

    if v_before is null then
      -- Product row missing — should not happen given the FK, but never
      -- silently skip a stock event; fail loudly instead.
      raise exception 'GATE:gate.handover.consumable_product_missing|Consumable product % not found for booking line %.', v_line.product_id, v_line.booking_line_id using errcode = 'P0001';
    end if;

    v_after := greatest(0, v_before - v_line.qty);
    -- Deliberately clamped at zero rather than raising: Handover has already
    -- happened by the time this trigger fires (it runs on the stage
    -- transition itself), so refusing here would block a completed handover
    -- over a stock-count discrepancy that predates this booking. A negative
    -- total_quantity going forward would be worse than a clamped one; the
    -- undercount is instead visible for a Manager to correct with
    -- adjust_stock() (0140), with the real reason on record.

    update products
       set total_quantity = v_after,
           updated_at = now()
     where id = v_line.product_id;

    insert into consumable_stock_movements (
      client_uuid, booking_id, booking_line_id, product_id,
      qty, quantity_before, quantity_after, created_by
    ) values (
      gen_random_uuid(), NEW.booking_id, v_line.booking_line_id, v_line.product_id,
      v_line.qty, v_before, v_after, NEW.actor_id
    );
  end loop;

  return NEW;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.recompute_unit_status(p_asset_id uuid)
 RETURNS inventory_state
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_new_status inventory_state;
  v_old_status inventory_state;
  v_retired_at timestamptz;
begin
  select status, retired_at into v_old_status, v_retired_at
  from product_units
  where id = p_asset_id;

  if not found then
    return null;
  end if;

  -- 1. Retired if product_units.retired_at is not null
  if v_retired_at is not null then
    v_new_status := 'Retired';

  -- 2. Missing if an open case (type = 'Missing', status not in ('Resolved', 'Closed', 'Cancelled')) links to this unit
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from cases c
    where c.type = 'Missing'
      and c.status not in ('Resolved', 'Closed', 'Cancelled')
      and (
        exists (select 1 from damage_findings df where df.case_id = c.id and df.unit_id = p_asset_id and df.voided_at is null)
        or
        (c.linked_booking_id is not null and exists (
          select 1 from booking_line_units blu
          join booking_lines bl on bl.id = blu.booking_line_id
          where bl.booking_id = c.linked_booking_id
            and blu.asset_id = p_asset_id
            and blu.unit_state = 'Missing'
        ))
      )
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Missing';

  -- 3. Maintenance if an unfinished maintenance row (completed_at is null) exists
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from maintenance_records mr
    where mr.product_unit_id = p_asset_id
      and mr.completed_at is null
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Maintenance';

  -- 4. On Rent if the unit is on a booking currently in On Rent stage
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from booking_line_units blu
    join booking_lines bl on bl.id = blu.booking_line_id
    join bookings b on b.id = bl.booking_id
    where blu.asset_id = p_asset_id
      and b.stage = 'On Rent'
      and b.cancelled_at is null
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'On Rent';

  -- 5. Returning if an unfinished Return session has accepted the unit but not completed
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from operation_sessions os
    where os.operation = 'Return'
      and os.state != 'Completed'
      and (
        exists (select 1 from session_line_movements slm where slm.session_id = os.id and slm.unit_id = p_asset_id)
        or exists (select 1 from booking_line_units blu where blu.return_session_id = os.id and blu.asset_id = p_asset_id)
      )
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Returning';

  -- 6. Inspection if on a Returned booking with no completed inspection
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from booking_line_units blu
    join booking_lines bl on bl.id = blu.booking_line_id
    join bookings b on b.id = bl.booking_id
    where blu.asset_id = p_asset_id
      and b.stage = 'Returned'
      and b.cancelled_at is null
      and (
        blu.condition is null
        or exists (
          select 1 from return_lines rl
          where rl.booking_line_id = bl.id
            and (rl.inspection_state != 'Inspected' or rl.inspected_at is null)
        )
      )
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Inspection';

  -- 7. Cleaning if in the cleaning queue and unfinished (cleaning_queue_entries.completed_at is null)
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from cleaning_queue_entries cqe
    where cqe.unit_id = p_asset_id
      and cqe.completed_at is null
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Cleaning';

  -- 8. Packed if packed on a booking currently in Packed stage
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from booking_line_units blu
    join booking_lines bl on bl.id = blu.booking_line_id
    join bookings b on b.id = bl.booking_id
    where blu.asset_id = p_asset_id
      and b.stage = 'Packed'
      and b.cancelled_at is null
      and blu.packed = true
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Packed';

  -- 9. Reserved if a live inventory_reservations row covers now() (period @> now() and released_at is null)
  elsif exists (
    select 1 from inventory_reservations ir
    where ir.asset_id = p_asset_id
      and ir.released_at is null
      and ir.period @> now()
  ) then
    v_new_status := 'Reserved';

  -- 10. Default: In Stock
  else
    v_new_status := 'In Stock';
  end if;

  -- Writes the result into product_units.status using transaction-scoped GUC
  if v_old_status is distinct from v_new_status then
    perform set_config('app.unit_status_recompute', 'on', true);
    update product_units
    set status = v_new_status,
        updated_at = now()
    where id = p_asset_id;
    perform set_config('app.unit_status_recompute', 'off', true);
  end if;

  return v_new_status;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.recompute_invoice_payment_state(p_invoice_id uuid)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_total_amount numeric(14,2);
  v_total_paid   numeric(14,2);
  v_reversed     numeric(14,2);
  v_outstanding  numeric(14,2);
  v_voided       timestamptz;
  v_status       invoice_status;
begin
  if p_invoice_id is null then
    return;
  end if;

  select total_amount, voided_at, status
    into v_total_amount, v_voided, v_status
    from invoices
   where id = p_invoice_id;

  if not found then
    return;
  end if;

  /*
   * A voided invoice is settled by a credit note, not by money moving. The old
   * function had no reference to `voided_at`, so a payment landing against a
   * voided invoice silently rewrote its status to 'Partially Paid' — un-voiding
   * it from a screen that never offered that action. `recordPayment` already
   * refuses this at the action layer; this is the same refusal at the row.
   */
  if v_voided is not null then
    return;
  end if;

  /*
   * ONLY 'Advance Payment' is revenue against the invoice.
   *   · 'Refund'          — money going the other way. Counting it as paid is
   *                         defect (a). A refund is recorded as a reversal.
   *   · 'Security Deposit' — a liability (Law 5). It has its own home in
   *                         `security_deposits` and must never touch
   *                         Outstanding. That is defect (b).
   */
  select coalesce(sum(p.amount), 0)
    into v_total_paid
    from payments p
   where p.invoice_id = p_invoice_id
     and p.status = 'Received'
     and p.payment_type = 'Advance Payment';

  /*
   * Net out every reversal written against those same payments. `payment_
   * reversals` has no `invoice_id` of its own — it points at the payment, and
   * the payment points at the invoice — so the join is the only route.
   */
  select coalesce(sum(r.amount), 0)
    into v_reversed
    from payment_reversals r
    join payments p on p.id = r.original_payment_id
   where p.invoice_id = p_invoice_id
     and p.status = 'Received'
     and p.payment_type = 'Advance Payment';

  v_total_paid  := greatest(0, v_total_paid - v_reversed);
  v_outstanding := greatest(0, v_total_amount - v_total_paid);

  update invoices
     set paid_amount        = v_total_paid,
         outstanding_amount = v_outstanding,
         status = case
           /* R-14, carried forward from 0080. A Draft is sticky: it keeps its
              status while money moves, and only an explicit issue action takes
              it out of Draft. Without this branch, R-02 (Draft for the whole
              rental) and R-03 (append damage lines at return) are mutually
              impossible — `reject_invoice_edit_after_issue` starts guarding the
              figures the moment the status leaves Draft. This clause must come
              FIRST; every branch below assumes the invoice is already issued. */
           when v_status = 'Draft'::invoice_status then v_status
           /* Fully settled. Guarded on total > 0 so a zero-value invoice is not
              declared Paid the moment it is created. */
           when v_outstanding = 0 and v_total_amount > 0 then 'Paid'::invoice_status
           when v_total_paid > 0 then 'Partially Paid'::invoice_status
           /* Money was here and has gone again — the reversal case. Without
              this clause a fully reversed invoice keeps status 'Paid' while
              carrying its full amount outstanding, which is the same lie in a
              different column. It returns to 'Sent', never to 'Draft': the
              invoice was issued and that fact does not un-happen. */
           when v_status in ('Paid'::invoice_status, 'Partially Paid'::invoice_status)
             then 'Sent'::invoice_status
           /* Draft / Sent / Overdue are left exactly as they were. */
           else v_status
         end,
         updated_at = now()
   where id = p_invoice_id;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.record_reservation_conflicts(p_detected_by text DEFAULT 'record_reservation_conflicts'::text)
 RETURNS integer
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_found integer := 0;
begin
  /*
   * A demand is a unit assigned to a booking that is live on the floor —
   * Booked, Packed or On Rent, not cancelled — for which no unreleased
   * reservation exists. `0100` writes one hold per assigned unit at the Booked
   * transition, so a missing hold means either the transition predates that
   * trigger or the GiST constraint refused it.
   *
   * Bookings with no lines at all are NOT conflicts. Production has three
   * (896, 825, 894), all empty shells from the Booqable import; they hold
   * nothing because they demand nothing, and filing them here would bury the
   * real rows under noise. The join to booking_line_units excludes them.
   */
  with demand as (
    select b.id as booking_id,
           l.id as booking_line_id,
           u.asset_id,
           tstzrange(b.pickup_at, b.return_at, '[)') as period
    from bookings b
    join booking_lines l      on l.booking_id = b.id
    join booking_line_units u on u.booking_line_id = l.id
    where b.stage in ('Booked', 'Packed', 'On Rent')
      and b.cancelled_at is null
      and u.asset_id is not null
      and not exists (
        select 1 from inventory_reservations r
        where r.booking_id = b.id
          and r.asset_id = u.asset_id
          and r.released_at is null
      )
  ),
  blamed as (
    select d.*,
           (select r.booking_id from inventory_reservations r
             where r.asset_id = d.asset_id
               and r.released_at is null
               and r.period && d.period
             limit 1) as blocking_booking_id
    from demand d
  )
  insert into reservation_backfill_conflicts
    (booking_id, booking_line_id, asset_id, period, blocking_booking_id, blocking_booking_no, detected_by)
  select bl.booking_id, bl.booking_line_id, bl.asset_id, bl.period, bl.blocking_booking_id,
         (select bb.booking_no from bookings bb where bb.id = bl.blocking_booking_id),
         p_detected_by
  from blamed bl
  /* Index inference, not `on constraint`: the target is a PARTIAL unique index,
     and Postgres will not accept an index name there. The predicate below must
     stay identical to the index's, or the inference silently fails to match. */
  on conflict (booking_id, asset_id) where resolved_at is null do nothing;

  get diagnostics v_found = row_count;
  return v_found;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.invoice_paid_net(p_invoice_id uuid)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
  /*
   * Only 'Advance Payment' is revenue against an invoice (MONEY-02):
   *   · 'Refund'          — money going the other way; counting it as paid is
   *                         the defect. payments_amount_positive forces
   *                         amount > 0, so an unfiltered sum RAISES paid.
   *   · 'Security Deposit' — a liability (Law 5), never touches Outstanding.
   *                         A live CHECK (payments_no_security_deposit) already
   *                         refuses the row; the filter is belt as well as
   *                         braces, and survives that CHECK being relaxed.
   * Less every reversal written against those same payments (Law 4: a payment
   * is immutable, a correction is a payment_reversals row). payment_reversals
   * has no invoice_id of its own, so the join through payments is the only
   * route.
   */
  select greatest(
    coalesce((
      select sum(p.amount) from payments p
       where p.invoice_id = p_invoice_id
         and p.status = 'Received'
         and p.payment_type = 'Advance Payment'
    ), 0)
    -
    coalesce((
      select sum(r.amount)
        from payment_reversals r
        join payments p on p.id = r.original_payment_id
       where p.invoice_id = p_invoice_id
         and p.status = 'Received'
         and p.payment_type = 'Advance Payment'
    ), 0),
    0);
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.intel_field_definition_archive_only()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
begin
  if old.archived_at is not null or new.archived_at is null
     or new.id is distinct from old.id or new.client_uuid is distinct from old.client_uuid
     or new.entity_type is distinct from old.entity_type or new.field_key is distinct from old.field_key
     or new.label is distinct from old.label or new.classification is distinct from old.classification
     or new.high_priority is distinct from old.high_priority or new.created_by is distinct from old.created_by
     or new.created_at is distinct from old.created_at then
    raise exception 'Custom field definitions are immutable; archive and create another';
  end if;
  return new;
end $function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.reject_update_daily_closing()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
begin
  -- The void is the one permitted transition, and only from live to voided.
  if OLD.voided_at is null and NEW.voided_at is not null then
    if row(NEW.*) is distinct from row(
      OLD.id, OLD.client_uuid, OLD.branch_id, OLD.business_date,
      OLD.counted_cash, OLD.expected_cash, OLD.variance, OLD.variance_reason,
      OLD.pickups_count, OLD.returns_count, OLD.new_count,
      OLD.collected_cash, OLD.collected_bank, OLD.collected_card, OLD.collected_other,
      OLD.receivables, OLD.deposits_held,
      OLD.approved_at, OLD.approved_by, OLD.created_at,
      NEW.voided_at, NEW.voided_by, NEW.void_reason
    ) then
      raise exception
        'A closing may only be VOIDED, not edited: the void may set voided_at/voided_by/void_reason and nothing else. Void this one and approve a corrected closing.';
    end if;
    return NEW;
  end if;

  raise exception
    'Closing % (branch %, %) is a signed record and is immutable. Void it and approve a corrected closing instead.',
    OLD.id, OLD.branch_id, OLD.business_date;
end;
$function$
